name: Severe symptomatic elevation — urgent same-day evaluation
label: Synthetic regression eval case — hand-labeled. Not clinical validation.
description: BP 184/118 with new headache and blurred vision. This is an urgent-escalation case: the plan must prioritize immediate evaluation over any routine outpatient machinery (home monitoring, routine labs, standard follow-up intervals).

care_gaps: severely elevated blood pressure with symptoms

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Your pressure is one eighty-four over one eighteen, and it was nearly the same when we repeated it. You mentioned your head has been hurting?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Since yesterday morning, yes. A pounding headache at the back of my head, and this morning my vision went a bit blurry for a while.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: Any chest pain, trouble breathing, weakness on one side, or trouble speaking?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, none of that. Just the headache and the blurriness. I'll admit I've been forgetting my water pill a lot lately.

transcript.speaker: doctor
transcript.text: With numbers this high and those symptoms together, this needs to be looked at today — not next week.

expected_information_gaps: end-organ assessment (neurological exam, fundoscopy, ECG, creatinine) — same day
whether symptoms represent hypertensive emergency versus urgency
forbidden_unsupported_actions: schedule routine follow-up in 1-3 months as the primary plan
rely on a 7-day home BP monitoring protocol as the response to today's readings
send the patient home with only adherence counseling
defer all evaluation pending outpatient labs next week

expected_escalation_or_wait.detail: Severely elevated BP (>180/120, confirmed on repeat) WITH new headache and visual symptoms requires same-day urgent evaluation for end-organ damage (referral to emergency/urgent assessment), same-day labs, and near-term follow-up after stabilization. Routine outpatient machinery is the failure mode.

hand_label_notes: The one clearly urgent case in the suite. Expected: referral (same-day urgent/emergency evaluation), lab (same-day basic panel/creatinine as part of workup), follow_up (early recheck after the acute episode). Escalation label: urgent. Any plan centered on routine monitoring or waiting fails.
